messages.subject: Re: Loading External Packages
messages.body_plain:
thanks Kevin-

i may have found a work around.  i installed the package into my packrat library.  if i need to update it i just copy and paste the package folder from my user library directory into my packrat library directory.  that seems to work on all updates that i've made so far.

> I am trying to run scripts in a packrat project and use an external library (MYPACKAGE).  i cannot get this to consistently work properly.  i have tried setting it as an external package in the Project options but when i do this i get the following error:
>
> packrat::set_opts(external.packages = c("MYPACKAGE"))
>
> Warning messages:
> 1: In Sys.junction(from, to) :
>   cannot set reparse point 'C:/Users/ericad/Documents/R working/PACKRATmyproject/packrat/lib-ext/MYPACKAGE', reason 'Access is denied'
> 2: In Sys.junction(from, to) :
>   cannot set reparse point '
> C:/Users/ericad/Documents/R working/PACKRATmyproject/packrat/lib-ext/Rcpp', reason 'Access is denied'
> 3: In Sys.junction(from, to) :
>   cannot set reparse point '
> C:/Users/ericad/Documents/R working/PACKRATmyproject/packrat/lib-ext/data.table', reason 'Access is denied'
> 4: In Sys.junction(from, to) :
>   cannot set reparse point '
> C:/Users/ericad/Documents/R working/PACKRATmyproject/packrat/lib-ext/plyr', reason 'Access is denied'
> 5: In Sys.junction(from, to) :
>   cannot set reparse point '
> C:/Users/ericad/Documents/R working/PACKRATmyproject/packrat/lib-ext/reshape2', reason 'Access is denied'
> 6: In Sys.junction(from, to) :

> C:/Users/ericad/Documents/R working/PACKRATmyproject/packrat/lib-ext/stringr', reason 'Access is denied'

>   The following external packages could not be linked into the packrat private library:
> - "MYPACKAGE", "Rcpp", "data.table", "plyr", "reshape2", "stringr"
>
>
> MYPACKAGE depends on having data.table, hence why it wants to access all of those other libraries.  Thing is, I already installed all of those libraries into my packrat library, with the exception of MYPACKAGE.  i have tried everything i can think of to make this work and it won't.  i wanted to keep MYPACKAGE external in case i made any changes to it.  I found that if i added MYPACKAGE to the packrat library using install_local that if i made changes to MYPACKAGE and tried to reinstall it, it would error out on me.  when i add MYPACKAGE as an external package through the project options i get a folder in packrat called lib-ext and it contains folders for MYPACKAGE plus the other packages.  Sometimes, after brut force manipulation of file directories and folders i can get it to work but once i close the project and re-open it i'm back right at the starting point of it not working.
>
> i have absolutely no clue why something that on the surface seems to be so simple is the most difficult thing to do.  Packrat is completely useless to me unless i can figure out how to do this AND do it consistently.

messages.subject: Packrat and knitr
messages.body_plain:
I have an automated report that i produce using knitr.  i'm running across the oddest problem.  I wrote a function that sums the data by month for several locations.  when i run this function in R i get the following result (which is correct):

     NAME MONTH      VOL
 1: TOTAL     1 13.00872
 2: TOTAL     2 11.62527
 3: TOTAL     3 12.71313
 4: TOTAL     4 12.67269
 5: TOTAL     5 15.05127
 6: TOTAL     6 14.61002
 7: TOTAL     7 15.43827
 8: TOTAL     8 15.22400
 9: TOTAL     9 14.91259
10: TOTAL    10 15.83505
11: TOTAL    11 14.97242
12: TOTAL    12 16.34950

when i run this same function (no changes) through knitr to produce the report i get the following result:

## NAME MONTH VOL
## 1: TOTAL 1 14.00872
## 2: TOTAL 2 13.62527
## 3: TOTAL 3 15.71313
## 4: TOTAL 4 16.11338
## 5: TOTAL 5 17.61269
## 6: TOTAL 6 18.46945
## 7: TOTAL 7 20.18851
## 8: TOTAL 8 21.04382
## 9: TOTAL 9 21.72287
## 10: TOTAL 10 23.54272
## 11: TOTAL 11 23.72971
## 12: TOTAL 12 26.03293

it is adding my MONTH to my original VOL column and producing a hybrid VOL column.  i have no explanation for why this is happening.  there is some transformation that is occuring between when i run R alone and when i run this through knitr to produce the report.  as an aside:  i have run this function through knitr outside of packrat and it works correctly.

messages.subject: Trouble with rJava and packrat
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to use Packrat for reproducible package management across Mac laptops and Ubuntu machines, and I'm having trouble with with the rJava package.

What I did:
- On the Mac, I navigated into an existing R project, opened the R CLI, and ran packrat::init(). There were no errors.
- I copied the R code and "packrat/packrat.lock" "packrat/packrat.opts" "packrat/src/" to the Ubuntu machine
- On the Ubuntu machine, I navigated into the R project directory, and started the R CLI

This fails with the following output:

The command failed with output:
* installing *source* package 'rJava' ...
** package 'rJava' successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
checking for gcc... gcc -std=gnu99
checking whether the C compiler works... yes
checking for C compiler default output file name... a.out
checking for suffix of executables...
checking whether we are cross compiling... no
checking for suffix of object files... o
checking whether we are using the GNU C compiler... yes
checking whether gcc -std=gnu99 accepts -g... yes
checking for gcc -std=gnu99 option to accept ISO C89... none needed
checking how to run the C preprocessor... gcc -std=gnu99 -E
checking for grep that handles long lines and -e... /bin/grep
checking for egrep... /bin/grep -E
checking for ANSI C header files... yes
checking for sys/wait.h that is POSIX.1 compatible... yes
checking for sys/types.h... yes
checking for sys/stat.h... yes
checking for stdlib.h... yes
checking for string.h... yes
checking for memory.h.
In addition: Warning message:
In restore(restart = FALSE) :
  The most recent snapshot was generated using R version 3.1.3

I've ensured that java is installed on the Ubuntu machine.

As a workaround, I also explored installing rJava directly via sudo apt-get install r-cran-rjava and then setting it as an external library.

I can successfully run library('rjava') outside of the packrat project.  But when I try to add it as an external library inside of the packrat project, I see

> packrat::set_opts(external.packages = c("rJava"))
Error in results[sapply(results, Negate(isTRUE))] :
  invalid subscript type 'list'
In addition: Warning message:
In symlinkExternalPackages(project = project) :
  The following external packages could not be located:
- 'rJava

Further investigation reveals that rJava is installed under /usr/lib/R/site-library/rJava but when I look at the libPaths in the packrat project, the site-library directory isn't there:

> .libPaths()
[1] "/srv/encrypted_fs/flatiron/code/bbirnbaum_r_packages/repo/blocks/blocks/pharma/analytics/research/Amgen_QA/packrat/lib/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/3.2.0"
[2] "/srv/encrypted_fs/flatiron/code/bbirnbaum_r_packages/repo/blocks/blocks/pharma/analytics/research/Amgen_QA/packrat/lib-ext"
[3] "/usr/lib/R/library"

What can I do to make rJava work?  Ideally, it would just work without the external package workaround, but even getting that to work would be ok.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Trouble with rJava and packrat
messages.body_plain:
Hi Benjamin,

One thing worth trying — can you install rJava manually from within R, e.g. with:
install.packages("rJava")

You may also need to run
sudo R CMD javareconf

after installing and updating Java, to ensure R is properly detecting the current available Java toolset.

Let me know if that helps!
Kevin
